```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load-model}
# Build the model once; the inline citation below reuses this object.
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Augustin_2023_warfarin_qsp"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
net_states <- setdiff(mod$state, c("depot", "central", "fibrin_auc"))
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1270443>
* Authors' code and data (SBML model files, parameter tables, simulated trial
  data): <https://github.com/DavAug/mipd-warfarin>

Augustin 2023 is a methods paper: it builds a *clinical-trial (CT) model* that
emulates warfarin treatment, uses it to simulate pre-MIPD phase I-III trials,
fits three model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) approaches to the simulated
data, and then compares those approaches in a simulated MIPD trial. The CT
model is the reusable pharmacometric artefact and is what this library entry
holds. It has five components (Section 2.1.2, Figure 1):

1. **Mechanistic model** -- the Wajima 2009 humoral coagulation network (51
   coagulation and vitamin K states) driven by one-compartment oral warfarin PK
   (Eq 6, Supplementary Tables S1.1-S1.3).
2. **Population model** -- Hartmann 2016 / 2020 normal IIV on ten
   coagulation-factor production rates, and Hamberg 2010 style lognormal IIV
   with CYP2C9, VKORC1 and age effects on the warfarin elimination rate, EC50
   and volume, extended to the two VKORC-catalysed vitamin K conversion rates
   (Eq S1.2-S1.9).
3. **Inter-occasion model** -- the vitamin K input rate is multiplied by a
   factor drawn from N(1, 0.1^2) each treatment day (Eq 7).
4. **Execution model** -- dose and sampling times are delayed by an
   exponentially distributed time with mean 30 min (Eq 8). This is a property of
   the event table, not of the model, and is implemented below.
5. **Measurement model** -- lognormal measurement error with scale 0.1 (Eq 9),
   carried by the model's `expSd` residual.

The three MIPD models of the paper (a neural-network regression, a deep
reinforcement-learning policy and a Hamberg 2010 PKPD model re-fitted by
hierarchical Bayesian inference) are not extracted: all three were trained on
data simulated from this CT model rather than on patient data, so they carry no
information about warfarin beyond what the CT model already holds.

# Population

The CT model is a simulator, not a fit, so its "population" is a virtual one.
Supplementary Table S1 lists the simulated cohorts: a phase I trial (N = 60,
single 10 mg dose, warfarin concentrations at 10, 35 and 60 h), a phase II
trial (N = 100, three weeks of INR-guided daily dosing) and a phase III trial
(N = 1000, eight weeks). CYP2C9 and VKORC1 genotype frequencies and ages were
modelled after Hamberg 2010 (phase III: CYP2C9 \*1\*1 66.1%, \*1\*2 18.4%,
\*1\*3 12.3%, \*2\*2 1.4%, \*2\*3 1.2%, \*3\*3 0.6%; VKORC1 GG 36.5%, GA 48.5%,
AA 15%; median age 50 years). The MIPD trial cohort (N = 1000, Figure 6) was
built the same way. The values the model uses were adopted from Wajima 2009,
Hartmann 2016 / 2020 and Hamberg 2010, and three of them were calibrated by
hand: the VKORC1 effect on the vitamin K conversion rates (against a plausible
baseline-INR distribution, Figure S1.1) and the VKORC1 GG EC50 and its IIV
(against 2543 IWPC maintenance doses, Figure S1.2).

The same information is available programmatically via `mod$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value is annotated in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Augustin_2023_warfarin_qsp.R` with the line of the
authors' parameter file it came from. The paper itself prints the model
structure (Tables S1.1-S1.3, Eq S1.1-S1.9) but defers the numeric values to the
deposited file `models/hartmann_coagulation_model_parameters.csv`; the ODE
right-hand sides were transcribed reaction by reaction from the deposited SBML
file `models/wajima_coagulation_model.xml` and agree with Table S1.1.

| Component | Model element | Value(s) | Source |
|-----------|---------------|----------|--------|
| PK structure | `depot` -> `central`, first-order `ka`, `kel` | -- | Eq 6; Section S1.1 |
| Absorption | `lka` | log(2) 1/h | csv `Pooled dose.absorption_rate`; Section S4.2 (Hamberg 2010 fixed ka = 2 1/h) |
| Volume | `lvc`, `etalvc` | 3.353 (28.6 L), log SD 0.054 | csv `central_warfarin.size` rows; Eq S1.7 |
| Elimination | `lkel`, `etalkel` | -3.716 (0.0243 1/h), log SD 0.071 | csv `elimination_rate_warfarin` rows; Eq S1.5-S1.6 |
| CYP2C9 on kel | `e_cyp2c9s2_kel`, `e_cyp2c9s3_kel` | 0.495, 0.757 (\*2\*2, \*3\*3; half per allele) | csv `Rel. elimination rate shift`; Eq S1.5 |
| Age on kel | `e_age_kel` | 0.00571 1/year, 1 - tanh(r (AGE - 71)) | csv; Eq S1.5 |
| Warfarin EC50 | `lec50`, `etalec50` | -2.0 (0.135 mg/L), log SD 0.1 | csv; Eq S1.3-S1.4; calibrated, Section S1.2 |
| VKORC1 on EC50 | `e_vkorc1aa_ec50` | 0.532 (AA vs GG; half per A allele) | csv; Eq S1.3 |
| Warfarin effect | `maximal_inhibitory_effect_warfarin`, `hill_warfarin` | 1, 1.15 | csv; Table S1.1 vitamin K equations; Section S4.4.2 |
| VK conversions | `lconversion_rate_vk_vkh2`, `lconversion_rate_vko_vk` | -3.781, -1.478; log SD 0.24 each | csv; Eq S1.8-S1.9 |
| VKORC1 on VK conversions | `e_vkorc1aa_vk_vkh2`, `e_vkorc1aa_vko_vk` | 0.2 each | csv; Section S1.2 (20% total reduction) |
| Production-rate IIV | `tvproduction_rate_*`, `etatvproduction_rate_*` | ten factors, SD = 20% of mean (V: 19.4%) | csv `Mean` / `Std.` rows; Eq S1.2 |
| Network rate constants | 136 parameters named as in Table S1.3 | see file | csv `Pooled global.*` rows |
| Initial concentrations | `bl_*` | csv amounts / 24 L | csv `Pooled central.*_amount` rows |
| Network ODEs | 51 states, 113 reactions | -- | SBML `wajima_coagulation_model.xml`; Table S1.1 |
| Fibrin integral | `d/dt(fibrin_auc) <- fibrin` | -- | Section S1.1.2 |
| Vitamin K IOV | `etaiov_vk_input_1` ... `_56` | variance 0.01 | Eq 7 |
| Measurement error | `expSd` | 0.1 | Eq 9; csv `Pooled Sigma log` |
| PT test | dilution 1:2, 300 nM TF, threshold 1500 nM*s, reference PT 11.8 s | -- | Section S1.1.2; deposited `model.py` |

# The prothrombin-time test

The INR is not an algebraic function of the model states. Following Section
S1.1.2, a blood sample (the state vector at the sampling time) is diluted 1:2
(all states divided by 3), thrombomodulin is removed, 300 nM tissue factor is
added, and the network is integrated in vitro with all external inputs and
non-vitamin-K-dependent production switched off. The prothrombin time (PT) is
the time at which the fibrin integral reaches 1500 nM*s; INR = PT / 11.8 s.

The authors' code performs the test with a reduced copy of the network
(`models/wajima_inr_test_model.xml`) that omits the reactions which cannot
proceed in the test tube. The helper below reproduces that exactly with a
second solve of the *same* model: the omitted reactions are switched off by
setting their rate constants to zero, and the sample is loaded with
replacement (`evid = 5`) events at time 0. The test integrates over 120 s on a
100-point grid and interpolates linearly, as the authors' code does.

**Solver.** All solves use `method = "lsoda"`. With rxode2's default
`liblsoda`, round-off of order 1e-20 nM in the activated factors is amplified
by the network's thrombin feedback loops (several half-maximal constants are
1e-4 nM) into a spurious coagulation burst under warfarin; `lsoda` does not do
this, and it is the configuration under which the gates below reproduce the
authors' own simulations.

```{r pt-test}
solve_method <- "lsoda"

# Rate constants of the reactions absent from the authors' in-vitro test model.
pt_zero_rates <- c(
  "complex_formation_rate_aii_tmod", "complex_formation_rate_apc_ps",
  "degradation_rate_aii_tmod_complex", "degradation_rate_apc_ps_complex",
  "degradation_rate_ca", "degradation_rate_d_dimer", "degradation_rate_fdp",
  "degradation_rate_kallikrein", "degradation_rate_pc", "degradation_rate_pc_activated",
  "degradation_rate_prekallikrein", "degradation_rate_ps", "degradation_rate_tmod",
  "degradation_rate_xf", "degradation_rate_xii", "degradation_rate_xii_activated",
  "input_rate_vk", "maximal_activation_rate_aii_tmod_complex_pc",
  "maximal_activation_rate_axii_xi", "maximal_activation_rate_ca_xii",
  "maximal_activation_rate_kallikrein_xii",
  "maximal_conversion_rate_apc_ps_complex_plasminogen",
  "maximal_conversion_rate_axii_prekallikrein",
  "maximal_degradation_rate_apc_ps_complex_av",
  "maximal_degradation_rate_apc_ps_complex_av_ax_complex",
  "maximal_degradation_rate_apc_ps_complex_aviii",
  "maximal_degradation_rate_apc_ps_complex_xf", "maximal_degradation_rate_plasmin_xf",
  "production_rate_fibrinogen", "tvproduction_rate_pc", "production_rate_plasminogen",
  "production_rate_prekallikrein", "tvproduction_rate_ps", "production_rate_tfpi",
  "production_rate_tmod", "tvproduction_rate_v", "production_rate_viii",
  "tvproduction_rate_xi", "tvproduction_rate_xii", "tvproduction_rate_xiii",
  "transition_rate_vk_central_to_peripheral", "transition_rate_vk_peripheral_to_central"
)

# Reference covariates for solves whose covariate-dependent parameters are
# irrelevant (the in-vitro test) or supplied directly through `params`.
add_reference_covariates <- function(ev) {
  ev$CYP2C9_S2_COUNT <- 0
  ev$CYP2C9_S3_COUNT <- 0
  ev$VKORC1_1639G_COUNT <- 2
  ev$AGE <- 71
  ev$OCC <- 0
  ev
}

# INR of each row of `samples` (one blood sample per row, network states as columns).
inr_test <- function(samples, standard_pt = 11.8, duration_s = 120) {
  n <- nrow(samples)
  grid_h <- seq(0, duration_s, length.out = 100) / 3600
  vals <- as.matrix(samples[, net_states]) / 3
  vals[, "tissue_factor"] <- 300
  vals[, "thrombomodulin"] <- 0
  vals <- cbind(vals, fibrin_auc = 0)
  load <- data.frame(
    id = rep(seq_len(n), each = ncol(vals)), time = 0, evid = 5L,
    cmt = rep(colnames(vals), times = n), amt = as.vector(t(vals))
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = rep(seq_len(n), each = length(grid_h)), time = rep(grid_h, n),
    evid = 0L, cmt = "fibrin_auc", amt = 0
  )
  ev <- rbind(load, obs)
  ev <- add_reference_covariates(ev[order(ev$id, ev$time, -ev$evid), ])
  th <- setNames(rep(0, length(pt_zero_rates)), pt_zero_rates)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, params = th, method = solve_method,
                       returnType = "data.frame")
  if (is.null(s$id)) s$id <- 1L
  threshold <- 1500 / 3600 # 1500 nM*s expressed in nM*h
  pt <- vapply(split(s, s$id), pt_from_curve, numeric(1), threshold = threshold)
  unname(pt) / standard_pt
}

# Time (s) at which the fibrin integral crosses the threshold; linear
# extrapolation from the last two grid points when the test is too short.
pt_from_curve <- function(d, threshold) {
  t_s <- d$time * 3600
  a <- d$fibrin_auc
  k <- length(a)
  if (a[k] < threshold) {
    return(t_s[k] + (threshold - a[k]) / ((a[k] - a[k - 1]) / (t_s[k] - t_s[k - 1])))
  }
  stats::approx(a, t_s, xout = threshold, ties = "ordered")$y
}
```

# Drug-free run-in and baseline INR

Simulations start from the Wajima initial concentrations. The authors run each
virtual patient drug-free for 100 days before the first dose so that the
network settles at the individual's own steady state (`warmup = 100` days in
the deposited trial scripts). For the typical patient the initial state is
already the steady state, and the typical baseline INR is 1.

```{r runin}
ev_runin <- add_reference_covariates(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 600, 1200, 2400), evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
)
runin <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_runin, method = solve_method, returnType = "data.frame")
runin |>
  select(time, coagulation_factor_ii, coagulation_factor_vii, coagulation_factor_x,
         fibrinogen, vitamin_k_hydroquinone) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Typical patient, drug-free: network states (nM).")

inr_baseline_typ <- inr_test(runin[runin$time == 2400, ])
inr_baseline_typ
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic: same parameters, same solver; measured drift < 1e-4 nM.
  max(abs(runin$coagulation_factor_ii / runin$coagulation_factor_ii[1] - 1)) < 1e-4,
  # The reference PT of 11.8 s is the typical network's own clotting time.
  abs(inr_baseline_typ - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# Gate 1: individual maintenance doses from the authors' deposit

The deposited file `maintenance_dose_distribution.csv` lists, for 1000 virtual
patients sampled from the population model, every individual parameter value
and the daily dose that the authors' optimiser found to give an INR of exactly
2.5 on day 20 (after the 100-day run-in, no inter-occasion variability, no
noise). This is the population that produced Figure S1.2. Twenty of those
patients (every 50th row, spanning all three VKORC1 genotypes) are embedded
below. Their individual parameters are passed to the model directly, so the
check exercises the network, the PK, the warfarin effect and the PT test
together: each patient's day-20 INR must come back as 2.5.

```{r maintenance-gate}
prod_names <- c("ii", "v", "vii", "ix", "x", "xi", "xii", "xiii", "pc", "ps")
pp <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(nrow(maint)),
  lvc = log(maint$vc), lkel = log(maint$kel), lec50 = log(maint$ec50),
  lconversion_rate_vk_vkh2 = log(maint$cvk), lconversion_rate_vko_vk = log(maint$cvko)
)
for (p in prod_names) pp[[paste0("tvproduction_rate_", p)]] <- maint[[paste0("p_", p)]]

ev_maint <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(nrow(maint)), each = 21),
             time = 2400 + 24 * rep(0:20, nrow(maint)), evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
             amt = rep(maint$dose, each = 21)),
  data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(maint)), time = 2400 + 20 * 24, evid = 0L,
             cmt = "central", amt = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  add_reference_covariates()

sim_maint <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_maint, params = pp, method = solve_method,
                             returnType = "data.frame")
day20 <- sim_maint[sim_maint$time == 2880, ]
maint_check <- maint |>
  transmute(
    id_deposit = id,
    VKORC1 = c("GG", "GA", "AA")[vkorc1 + 1],
    CYP2C9 = c("*1/*1", "*1/*2", "*1/*3", "*2/*2", "*2/*3", "*3/*3")[cyp2c9 + 1],
    dose_mg = dose,
    inr_day20 = inr_test(day20)
  )
knitr::kable(maint_check, digits = 4,
             caption = "Day-20 INR at the deposited maintenance dose (target 2.5).")
stopifnot(
  nrow(day20) == nrow(maint),
  # Same individual parameters on both sides, so only solver and optimiser
  # tolerance separate them: measured maximum deviation 8e-5.
  max(abs(maint_check$inr_day20 - 2.5)) < 0.002
)
```

# Gate 2: phase I trial (warfarin PK)

The phase I trial (Algorithm S1) gives 60 patients a single 10 mg dose and
measures warfarin concentrations at 10, 35 and 60 h, with exponentially
delayed dosing and sampling and lognormal measurement error. The patients'
covariates and the 5th-95th percentiles of the deposited simulated
concentrations (`trial_phase_I.csv`) are embedded below; the packaged model is
simulated with fresh random draws for the same patients.

```{r phase1}
"), sep = ":", col.names = c("id", "cyp2c9", "vkorc1", "age"))
p1_ref <- data.frame(
  time = rep(c(10, 35, 60), each = 5),
  q = rep(c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), 3),
  conc = c(0.2420, 0.2580, 0.2782, 0.3039, 0.3328,
           0.1275, 0.1498, 0.1668, 0.1850, 0.2393,
           0.0667, 0.0758, 0.0939, 0.1138, 0.1633)
)
cyp_s2 <- c(0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0)
cyp_s3 <- c(0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2)

set.seed(2023)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)
n1 <- nrow(p1_cov)
delay_dose <- rexp(n1, rate = 1 / 0.5)
ev_p1 <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n1), time = delay_dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", amt = 10),
  data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(n1), each = 3),
             time = rep(c(10, 35, 60), n1) + rexp(3 * n1, rate = 1 / 0.5),
             evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(
    CYP2C9_S2_COUNT = cyp_s2[p1_cov$cyp2c9[id] + 1],
    CYP2C9_S3_COUNT = cyp_s3[p1_cov$cyp2c9[id] + 1],
    VKORC1_1639G_COUNT = 2 - p1_cov$vkorc1[id],
    AGE = p1_cov$age[id], OCC = 0
  )
sim_p1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_p1, method = solve_method, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(nominal = c(10, 35, 60)[findInterval(time, c(0, 30, 55))],
         conc = Cc * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, 0.1)))
p1_sim_q <- sim_p1 |>
  group_by(nominal) |>
  reframe(q = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), conc_sim = quantile(conc, q))
p1_cmp <- p1_ref |>
  left_join(p1_sim_q, by = c("time" = "nominal", "q")) |>
  mutate(ratio = conc_sim / conc)
p1_cmp |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = time, names_from = q, values_from = c(conc, conc_sim)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Warfarin concentration (mg/L) percentiles: deposited phase I data (conc_) vs this model (conc_sim_).")

ggplot(sim_p1, aes(nominal, conc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, position = position_jitter(width = 1)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(p1_ref, q == 0.5), aes(time, conc), colour = "red") +
  geom_line(data = filter(p1_ref, q %in% c(0.05, 0.95)), aes(time, conc, group = q),
            colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Warfarin concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = "Points: this model. Red: median and 5th/95th percentiles of the authors' phase I data (Figure 5, left panel).")

stopifnot(
  # Centre: a wrong volume, clearance or covariate coding moves the medians by
  # tens of percent; with n = 60 the sampling error of a median is ~3-5%.
  all(abs(log(p1_cmp$ratio[p1_cmp$q == 0.5])) < 0.10),
  # Spread: interquartile percentiles within 15%.
  all(abs(log(p1_cmp$ratio[p1_cmp$q %in% c(0.25, 0.75)])) < 0.15)
)
```

# Gate 3: phase II trial (INR under INR-guided dosing)

The phase II trial (Algorithm S2, Figure 5 middle panel) treats 100 patients
for three weeks: 10, 7.5 and 5 mg on days 0-2, then the dose is adjusted on
days 3, 5, 7 and 13 whenever the INR measured that morning is outside 2-3,
using `dose * 2.5 / INR` rounded to what tablets allow (0, 1, 2 mg or a
multiple of 0.5 mg, at most 30 mg; `adjust_dosing_regimen()` in the authors'
`3_perform_trial_phase_2.py`). INR is measured before dosing on days 0, 1, 2,
3, 5, 7, 13 and 20. The trial is re-run here for the same 100 patients
(covariates from the deposited `trial_phase_II.csv`, embedded below) with
fresh draws of the IIV, the daily vitamin K factor, the execution delays and
the measurement error, and with the dose adjustments made by the same rule on
this model's own INR measurements. The INR quartiles on each measurement day
and the quartiles of the dose chosen on day 13 are compared with the deposited
trial.

```{r phase2-data}
  day = rep(c(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 20), each = 3),
  q = rep(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), 8),
  inr = c(0.954, 1.083, 1.187, 1.241, 1.396, 1.629, 1.491, 1.683, 1.970,
          1.603, 1.815, 2.101, 1.893, 2.170, 2.486, 2.203, 2.510, 2.833,
```

```{r phase2-sim}
# Dose update of the authors' phase II script: only outside the therapeutic
# range, rounded to tablet strengths, capped at 30 mg.
adjust_dose <- function(dose, inr, target = 2.5) {
  out <- dose
  move <- inr < 2 | inr > 3
  d <- dose[move] * target / inr[move]
  d <- ifelse(d < 0.5, 0, ifelse(d < 1.5, 1, ifelse(d < 2.25, 2, round(2 * d) / 2)))
  out[move] <- pmin(d, 30)
  out
}

n2 <- nrow(p2)
meas_days <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 20)
adjust_days <- c(3, 5, 7, 13)

# One fixed random draw per patient, re-used by every sequential solve below so
# the patient is the same person each time the trial is re-simulated.
set.seed(4)
omega_sd <- sqrt(diag(mod$omega))
etas <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(n2 * length(omega_sd)), n2) %*% diag(omega_sd))
names(etas) <- names(omega_sd)
delay <- matrix(rexp(n2 * 21, rate = 1 / 0.5), n2, 21) # days 0-20, one per day
eps <- matrix(rnorm(n2 * length(meas_days), 0, mod$theta[["expSd"]]), n2)
pars_p2 <- cbind(id = seq_len(n2), etas)

p2_events <- function(doses, last_day) {
  dose_rows <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(n2), each = 20), day = rep(0:19, n2),
                          evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", amt = as.vector(t(doses)))
  obs_rows <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(n2), each = 8), day = rep(meas_days, n2),
                         evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    filter(day <= last_day) |>
    # INR is sampled just before that day's (equally delayed) dose
    mutate(time = 2400 + 24 * day + delay[cbind(id, day + 1)] - ifelse(evid == 0L, 1e-6, 0),
           OCC = day + 1) |>
    bind_rows(data.frame(id = seq_len(n2), day = -1, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
                         amt = 0, time = 0, OCC = 0)) |>
    mutate(CYP2C9_S2_COUNT = cyp_s2[p2$cyp2c9[id] + 1],
           CYP2C9_S3_COUNT = cyp_s3[p2$cyp2c9[id] + 1],
           VKORC1_1639G_COUNT = 2 - p2$vkorc1[id],
           AGE = p2$age[id]) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

p2_inr <- function(doses, last_day) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, p2_events(doses, last_day), params = pars_p2,
                       method = solve_method, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "day")
  s <- s[s$day >= 0, ]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(s$coagulation_factor_ii))
  s$inr <- inr_test(s) * exp(eps[cbind(s$id, match(s$day, meas_days))])
  s
}

doses <- matrix(rep(c(10, 7.5, 5, rep(5, 17)), each = n2), n2)
for (d in adjust_days) {
  s <- p2_inr(doses, d)
  inr_d <- s$inr[s$day == d][order(s$id[s$day == d])]
  doses[, (d + 1):20] <- adjust_dose(doses[, d], inr_d)
}
samp <- p2_inr(doses, 20)

p2_cmp <- samp |>
  group_by(day) |>
  reframe(q = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), inr_sim = quantile(inr, q)) |>
  left_join(p2_ref, by = c("day", "q")) |>
  mutate(ratio = inr_sim / inr)
p2_cmp |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = day, names_from = q, values_from = c(inr, inr_sim)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "INR quartiles by trial day: deposited phase II data (inr_) vs this model (inr_sim_).")

dose13 <- data.frame(q = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
                     deposited = quantile(p2$d13, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)),
                     simulated = quantile(doses[, 14], c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)))
knitr::kable(dose13, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Quartiles of the dose (mg) given from day 13 onwards.")

ggplot(samp, aes(day, inr, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = filter(p2_ref, q == 0.5), aes(day, inr, group = NULL), colour = "red") +
  geom_line(data = filter(p2_ref, q != 0.5), aes(day, inr, group = q), colour = "red",
            linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(2, 3), colour = "blue", linetype = 3) +
  labs(x = "Day of treatment", y = "INR",
       caption = "Grey: this model, one line per patient. Red: median and quartiles of the authors' phase II data (Figure 5, middle panel). Blue: therapeutic range.")

stopifnot(
  # Centre: an EC50, VKORC1 or network transcription error shifts the median
  # INR trajectory by far more than the ~5% sampling error of n = 100.
  all(abs(log(p2_cmp$ratio[p2_cmp$q == 0.5])) < 0.10),
  # Quartiles within 15% on every measurement day.
  all(abs(log(p2_cmp$ratio)) < 0.15),
  # The titrated dose is the trial's integrated readout of sensitivity.
  abs(log(dose13$simulated[2] / dose13$deposited[2])) < 0.2
)
```

# PKNCA: single-dose warfarin PK by CYP2C9 genotype

The paper reports no NCA. As a check of the PK layer, a single 10 mg dose is
simulated without IIV for a 71-year-old in each CYP2C9 genotype group, and the
NCA half-life is compared with the model's own log(2) / kel.

```{r pknca}
geno <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("*1/*1", "*1/*2", "*1/*3", "*2/*2", "*2/*3", "*3/*3"),
  CYP2C9_S2_COUNT = cyp_s2, CYP2C9_S3_COUNT = cyp_s3
)
tgrid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 168, 240, 336)
ev_nca <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(6), time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", amt = 10),
  data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(6), each = length(tgrid)), time = rep(tgrid, 6), evid = 0L,
             cmt = "central", amt = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(CYP2C9_S2_COUNT = geno$CYP2C9_S2_COUNT[id], CYP2C9_S3_COUNT = geno$CYP2C9_S3_COUNT[id],
         VKORC1_1639G_COUNT = 2, AGE = 71, OCC = 0)
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_nca, method = solve_method, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(treatment = geno$treatment[id])

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(filter(sim_nca, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(6), time = 0, amt = 10, treatment = geno$treatment),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
kel_typ <- exp(mod$theta[["lkel"]]) *
  (1 - (mod$theta[["e_cyp2c9s2_kel"]] * geno$CYP2C9_S2_COUNT +
          mod$theta[["e_cyp2c9s3_kel"]] * geno$CYP2C9_S3_COUNT) / 2)
nca_tab <- nca_tab |>
  left_join(data.frame(treatment = geno$treatment, thalf_model = log(2) / kel_typ),
            by = "treatment")
nca_tab |>
  rename("CYP2C9" = treatment, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
         "AUC0-inf (h*mg/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 NCA (h)" = half.life,
         "t1/2 = log(2)/kel (h)" = thalf_model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Single 10 mg dose, typical 71-year-old, VKORC1 GG.")
stopifnot(
  # Terminal phase is mono-exponential in kel once absorption (ka = 2 1/h) is over.
  all(abs(nca_tab$half.life / nca_tab$thalf_model - 1) < 0.02),
  # AUC = dose / (kel * V) for a one-compartment model.
  all(abs(nca_tab$aucinf.obs / (10 / (kel_typ * exp(mod$theta[["lvc"]]))) - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Parameter source.** The paper prints the model structure but not the
  parameter values; it points to the authors' GitHub repository for them. All
  values were taken from `models/hartmann_coagulation_model_parameters.csv`
  (repository commit `4710c062`), using the population-model rows ("Pooled",
  "Log mean", "Log std.", "Mean", "Std.", "Rel. ... shift") rather than the
  deterministic rows at the top of the file. The two differ only in the
  absorption rate (pooled 2 1/h, the Hamberg 2010 value cited in Section S4.2,
  vs 1 1/h).
* **Fixed parameters.** Every value is wrapped in `fixed()` because the CT
  model was assembled and hand-calibrated, never estimated.
* **Production-rate IIV.** Eq S1.2 gives normal IIV with SD = 20% of the mean.
  It is encoded as `rate = mean * (1 + eta)` with variance (SD / mean)^2,
  which is the same distribution. The deposited SD for factor V is 0.223 for a
  mean of 1.15 (19.4%), and that value is used.
* **Inter-occasion variability.** The daily vitamin K factor is encoded as one
  eta per treatment day for days 1-56 (`OCC` = treatment day), the longest
  simulated trial. Records with `OCC = 0`, or beyond day 56, carry none.
* **Execution model.** The exponential dose and sampling delays (Eq 8) belong
  to the event table and are generated in the gates above, not in the model.
* **Dose input.** The authors approximate an oral dose by a 0.01 h infusion
  into the dose compartment (Section S1.1.1); the gates use a bolus into
  `depot`, which differs by less than the solver tolerance after a few minutes.
* **INR.** The PT test needs a second solve, so the INR cannot be an output of
  the model itself; the helper `inr_test()` above implements Section S1.1.2 as
  the authors' code does, including their use of a reduced reaction set in the
  test tube, rather than the prose description that sets all production rates
  to zero (the vitamin K-dependent production retained by the code changes the
  120 s test negligibly).
* **Volume of distribution.** The typical volume, 28.6 L, is twice the Hamberg
  2010 S-warfarin volume of 14.3 L. The paper does not say whether the dose
  should be read as racemic warfarin or as S-warfarin; the gates use the doses
  exactly as the authors' trial scripts did.
* **VKORC1 coding.** The paper writes the genotype as GG / GA / AA; this is
  mapped to `VKORC1_1639G_COUNT` (2 / 1 / 0).
